title: Add response-fidelity metering and anchored observability playbook
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Add response fidelity metric and playbook: new telemetry for token-level output fidelity, dashboard and alert tuning guidance. No breaking API changes.
description:
Motivation: We frequently see noisy alert churn driven by model output variability (paraphrasing, hallucination spikes, and template drift). Existing token-cost and latency signals are useful, but they do not capture whether the model's responses stayed within expected structural/semantic shape. This PR introduces a lightweight response-fidelity meter (per-invocation and per-token signals) and an anchored observability playbook that ties fidelity degradations to concrete investigation steps and automated mitigations.

What this PR does (single continuous description): Adds a production-safe response_fidelity score emitted with every generation invocation (0-100 scaled integer) computed from a small ensemble of shape-check heuristics and optional reference-set similarity; exposes per-token fidelity deltas for long-tail investigations; exposes a high-cardinality label set (route, model_variant, prompt_shape_hash, tenant_id) with careful sampling to limit cardinality. Adds a new Grafana dashboard (response fidelity overview + long-tail investigator panel), an SLO/alert bundle with graduated thresholds and auto-muted noisy tenants, and documentation + runbook for on-call. Also includes a short experimental hook that allows routing to a lower-latency fallback model when fidelity falls below a configured threshold.

Checklist:
- [x] Instrumentation: emit fidelity scores to tracing and metrics pipelines
- [x] Dashboard + panels: overview, cohort heatmap, long-tail explorer
- [x] Alerts: SLO-based alert + tenant auto-suppress playbook
- [x] Unit & integration tests for meter logic and pipeline wiring
- [x] Docs and runbook: docs/observability/response-fidelity.md
- [x] Rolling deploy plan: feature-flagged by default for 48h canary

Implementation notes: The fidelity meter lives in src/observability/response_fidelity_meter.py. It uses a set of deterministic shape checks (prefix/suffix tokens, bracket balancing, JSON schema sparse checks) and an optional lightweight embedding similarity score against a curated reference set stored in telemetry/reference-anchors. The metric is computed synchronously but capped to a 0.5ms median overhead on our baseline workloads; heavy similarity work is sampled at 1% by default and runs asynchronously. To avoid cardinality explosions we emit the detailed per-token delta only to the sampled trace (tracing tag response.fidelity.token_deltas) and aggregate a compact histogram (fidelity.delta_hist) for metrics rollups.

Backward compatibility & privacy: No public API contract changes. The fidelity value is considered telemetry; content is hashed before being stored in long-term reference buckets and PII checks run during sampling. See docs for KMS/privacy notes.

Related Linear/Jira: ENG-2483 (core meter), PM-1311 (playbook), SUP-912 (customer incident that motivated the change).

Testing & canary: Adds unit tests (tests/test_response_fidelity.py) and an integration scenario in perf-canary that replays 10k prompts with seeded degradations. The feature is behind a runtime feature flag (feature.observability.response_fidelity) and will be enabled for 5% traffic during the initial rollout window.

Links: Linear: https://linear.app/company/issue/ENG-2483, Runbook (draft): docs/observability/response-fidelity.md

review_comments:
Diego Martinez (reviewer): Please call out the privacy guarantees for sampled content and confirm KMS usage. Also flagged a potential high-cardinality tag (prompt_shape_hash) — can we cap cardinality or add a regex sanitization?

Author (Ava Chen): Reply: privacy note added to docs; sampled content is hashed with customer KMS when configured and we added a cap/sanitizer layer for prompt_shape_hash (max unique shapes per tenant = 1000 by default). Updated telemetry/metrics_mappers.py to apply truncation + hashing.

Sana Iqbal (reviewer): Suggest tuning alert thresholds and adding an auto-suppression window for noisy tenants — proposed a two-stage alert (warning @5m, page @30m) and suggested adding tenant-level mute after repeated noise.

Author: Implemented two-stage alert in alerts/response_fidelity_slo.yaml and added auto-mute logic to the playbook.

Tomás Alvarez (reviewer): Asked for a lightweight dashboard panel that surfaces worst-performing prompt shapes and their exemplar traces.

Author: Added long-tail explorer panel that links to sampled traces and exposes an example invocation for each shape.

Final approval: Diego approved after privacy & cardinality changes; Sana approved after threshold adjustments.

merge: Merged via squash on 2026-03-05 by Diego Martinez. Merge commit message: 'Add response fidelity metering, dashboard, alerts, and playbook. Feature-flagged rollout.' Rollout: feature flag enabled at 5% traffic for 48h, then 20% for 72h, then gradual rollout with auto-mute safeguards. Post-merge actions: monitor fidelity.delta_hist and SLO error budget for 72h; if noisy tenants exceed threshold, auto-mute logic will suppress alerts and create a ticket for customer success to investigate.
notes: Operational guidance in docs/observability/response-fidelity.md includes an investigation checklist, suggested thresholds per model family, and a small troubleshooting section for false positives. Also added a sample notebook in examples/ for teams to reproduce fidelity scoring locally.
